correctness.rationale: For q>0 the j-th column sum of the nonnegative mean matrix is L_j, independently of w. For a nonnegative Perron vector normalized to sum one, the spectral radius is therefore the weighted average of the L_j with that vector's weights. Every index with w_i>0 has positive Perron-vector coordinate since the rank-one term at that row is strictly positive on any nonzero nonnegative vector and the radius is positive. Thus equality forces w to be supported on maximizing lines. Conversely the block on that support is invariant and has all column sums equal to the maximum, so realizes it. This avoids any irreducibility assumption. At q=0 the matrix is independent of w and diagonal. The envelope of distinct affine lines uses each on at most one interval; increasing active slopes give at most n−1 interior genuine switches, with coincident lines not counted as switches. In the sharp construction s_i remains above 5/8 and b_i below 1/2; the inequality n(2−s_i)>b_i(i+1) gives strict germination ordering. The signed pairwise difference δ(i−j)[2nq−(i+j+1)] verifies each unique winner interval and exactly two tied adjacent classes at each crossing. The three-depth crossings and values agree. The result is about the spectral radius of the specified mean projection; growth from an initial state absent from all accessible maximal components and almost-sure stochastic growth are not asserted. The finite rational tests in the frozen package are corroboration, not needed for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The complete allocation picture is useful in the specified baseline mean model: mixtures never strictly improve the spectral objective, yet every tie has an exact simplex face of optima. The monotone admissible family shows that the deepest-to-shallowest tradeoff does not force the number of changes to stay small: every class can be uniquely optimal on its own interval. This sharp policy sensitivity is the useful part beyond the textbook spectral bound, without suggesting that stochastic populations obey the same rule.
